2608.21544.title: Forgotten in Weights, Recovered by Tools: Agentic Tool Unlearning for LLM Agents
2608.21544.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as tool-augmented agents, where responses can depend on tool calls and external observations rather than model parameters alone. This creates an evaluation mismatch for LLM unlearning: previous unlearning methods may suppress direct parametric recall, but an agent can still recover the same forget target through tools such as web search, retrieval, or database lookup. We identify this failure mode as tool-mediated recovery and study agentic tool unlearning, which aims to reduce both parametric recall and tool-mediated recovery while preserving normal tool use for retained knowledge. To address this challenge, we propose Agentic Tool Unlearning (ATU), a two-stage framework. The first stage applies parametric knowledge unlearning to suppress direct recall, while the second stage performs trajectory-level reinforcement learning in simulated tool-augmented environments to penalize target-seeking tool behavior and final-answer leakage. Experiments on RWKU and MUSE across different LLM architectures show that ATU achieves a better balance between target forgetting and retained utility, making unlearning more robust under tool-augmented agent deployment.
2608.21544.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被部署為工具增強代理，其中回應可能依賴於工具調用和外部觀察，而不僅僅是模型參數。這為LLM的忘記評估創造了不匹配的情況：之前的忘記方法可能會抑制直接的參數回憶，但代理仍然可以通過網絡搜索、檢索或數據庫查詢等工具恢復相同的忘記目標。我們將這種失敗模式識別為工具介導的恢復，並研究代理工具忘記，旨在減少參數回憶和工具介導的恢復，同時保留對保留知識的正常工具使用。為了應對這一挑戰，我們提出了代理工具忘記（ATU），這是一個兩階段框架。第一階段應用參數知識忘記以抑制直接回憶，而第二階段則在模擬的工具增強環境中執行軌跡級別的強化學習，以懲罰尋找目標的工具行為和最終答案洩漏。在不同LLM架構下對RWKU和MUSE的實驗顯示，ATU在目標遺忘和保留效用之間達到了更好的平衡，使得在工具增強代理部署下的忘記變得更加穩健。
